general_notes.general_notes:
The study is a direct replication of Wolfers et al. (2018), using the same analytical pipeline on two new independent samples. The entire analytical pipeline is made publicly available.

- deviation_metric: "Z-score. Extreme deviations defined as |Z| > 2.6 (p < .005), with sensitivity analyses at |Z| > 1.96 and |Z| > 3.1. Also extreme value statistics."
- association_analysis: "Nonparametric tests (Mann-Whitney) for group differences in the percentage of extreme deviations. Correlations between extreme deviations and PANSS scores."
- key_findings_brief: "Group-level differences in brain structure disguise considerable individual differences in brain aberrations in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder."
- key_findings_detailed: "The study replicated previous findings showing robust group-level gray matter differences between patients (schizophrenia and bipolar disorder) and healthy controls. However, at the individual level, the spatial patterns of extreme brain structure deviations were highly heterogeneous, with only a small percentage of patients showing abnormalities in the same brain regions. Extreme negative deviations were more prevalent in schizophrenia than in healthy controls and were correlated with symptom severity (PANSS scores)."
- key_limitations: "The study used only structural MRI, and other modalities might show more homogeneity. The sample was predominantly adult, while schizophrenia often onsets in adolescence. The handling of multi-site data could be improved in the future."
- application_notes: "The findings support the need for individualized analyses in psychiatry instead of focusing on group studies, as group differences say little about the individual patient's brain deviations."
